physical_harm: Firearm wounds on the head, chest and right upper arm, multiple abrasions and contusions, death due to shock and haemorrhage
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 302, 147, 148 and 149 IPC; upheld under Sections 304-Part I, 147, 148 and 149 IPC
premeditation_planning: Not found; incident happened on the spur of the moment in an uncontrollable, embittered and agitated state of enragement
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence of the eye witnesses showed that they have with noteworthy consistency and cohesion authenticated the case of the prosecution in all material particulars, they have identified as well the appellants and their co-accused and also have provided graphic details of the events in the sequence in which the same unfolded at the place of occurrence. The testimony of the doctor who performed post mortem on the dead body (PW-5) reveals firearm wounds on the head, chest and right upper arm of the deceased together with the multiple abrasions and contusions on various parts of the body.
witness_credibility: The eye witnesses have with noteworthy consistency and cohesion authenticated the case of the prosecution in all material particulars, they have identified as well the appellants and their co-accused and also have provided graphic details of the events in the sequence in which the same unfolded at the place of occurrence.

legal_representation.accused: Dr. J. P. Dhanda, Ms. Raj Rani Dhanda, Vineet Dhanda, N. A. Usmani, Mohd. Shahid Hussain
legal_representation.state: Ravi Prakash Mehrotra, V. S. Shukla, Vibhu Tiwari

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.high_court: Modified conviction to Section 304-Part I IPC, sentence reduced to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and fine of Rs.5000/-
appeal_history.supreme_court: Partly allowed the appeal, reduced sentence to rigorous imprisonment for 7 years

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons formed an unlawful assembly and jointly launched a lethal attack on the deceased using a firearm, resulting in his death. The incident occurred after a series of altercations between the deceased and the accused persons, leading to the deceased being shot and assaulted.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove that the accused persons were the aggressors who assaulted the deceased, and that the deceased and his cohorts attacked the accused persons, prompting the accused to defend themselves with a firearm. They also claimed that there was no pre-meditation or prior concert on the part of the accused persons.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the absence of pre-meditation or prior concert, coupled with the uncontrollable and agitated state of the accused persons, may mitigate the sentence.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the absence of pre-meditation or prior concert, the uncontrollable and agitated state of the accused persons, their lack of infamous criminal background, and the passage of more than three decades since the incident.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court weighed the absence of pre-meditation or prior concert, the uncontrollable and agitated state of the accused persons, their lack of infamous criminal background, and the passage of more than three decades since the incident.
other_sentence_order: The court reduced the sentence for the offence under Section 304-Part I/149 IPC to rigorous imprisonment for 7 years, while affirming the other sentences.
